newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 3.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Certain domestic producers would welcome a devaluation of the Czech crown as a way to boost exports.
- The government yesterday passed a motion to import 53 billion cubic metres of Norwegian natural gas over a period of twenty years.
- Tax revenues were down by approximately one fifth during the first quarter of this year. While corporate tax revenues in March reflected expectations, revenues from private citizens were down.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The government wants to raise bank deposit rates as a way of compensating citizens for the freezing of wage increases.
- Various government officials and economic experts oppose raising tariffs or other barriers on imports as a way of decreasing consumer demand in the Czech Republic.

- Industry and trade minister, Vladimir Dlouhy announced yesterday that the Temelin nuclear plant will not go online until the year 1999, and will cost around 76 billion crowns to complete, an increase of 10 percent.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Agrobanka which is under forced administration has begun issuing loans to private individuals. The solovent portion of the bank is to be sold to a foreign investor.
PRAVO - The Investicni a postovni banka (IPB) bought nearly six percent of Plzensky Prazdroj from Ceska pojistovna, raising its stake in the brewery to 17.6 percent.
